tasks.spec:
You are a code-feature worker implementing Phase 1 (client-side crypto & encrypted storage) of MonetaFox Reborn, a Microsoft Money replacement PWA. The repository is an existing, committed Vite + React 19 + TypeScript project at /home/user/Source/MonetaFoxReborn (the REPO). Read plan-reborn.md (Phase 1) and spec.md (User Accounts & Security) in the REPO first.

BOUNDARY / OWNERSHIP: Edit files directly in the REPO working tree. You OWN only these paths: src/lib/crypto/** (create it), the .husky/pre-commit hook (one-line fix, see below), and package.json (only to add the fake-indexeddb devDependency). Do NOT modify any other source, do NOT touch the four planning .md files, do NOT touch anything under .ringer/, do NOT git commit and do NOT git push (leave changes uncommitted for the reviewer). Do NOT add dependencies other than fake-indexeddb.

DELIVERABLE — implement client-side encryption with the EXACT public API below (the reviewer runs a hidden contract test against these signatures; drift will fail it):

1. src/lib/crypto/keyDerivation.ts
   - export type EncryptionMode = 'basic' | 'advanced'
   - export const PBKDF2_ITERATIONS: number   // >= 100000
   - export type KeyInput = { mode: 'basic'; email: string; password: string; entropy?: Uint8Array } | { mode: 'advanced'; passphrase: string; salt: string }
   - export async function deriveKey(input: KeyInput): Promise<CryptoKey>
     * BASIC: PBKDF2 over (password bytes, and if entropy is provided append/mix those bytes into the input keying material), salt = NORMALIZED email (lowercased + trimmed) encoded to bytes, PBKDF2_ITERATIONS, SHA-256, deriving a 256-bit AES-GCM key (usages: encrypt, decrypt). Normalization means the same identity with different case/whitespace derives the SAME key when entropy is absent.
     * ADVANCED: PBKDF2 over passphrase bytes, salt = provided salt string bytes, same params, same AES-GCM 256 key.

2. src/lib/crypto/CryptoStore.ts  (AES-GCM)
   - export async function encrypt(key: CryptoKey, plaintext: string): Promise<string>
     * Generate a fresh random 12-byte IV via crypto.getRandomValues per call; return base64 of (iv concatenated with ciphertext). Two encrypts of the same plaintext must differ.
   - export async function decrypt(key: CryptoKey, payload: string): Promise<string>
     * Reverse it; AES-GCM authentication must make a wrong key or tampered payload REJECT (throw).

3. src/lib/crypto/EncryptedTable.ts  (transparent Dexie encryption)
   - export class EncryptedTable<T extends Record<string, unknown>>
     * constructor(table: Dexie.Table<any, any>, key: CryptoKey)
     * async add(item: T): Promise<any>            // stores { <primaryKey?>, _enc: <ciphertext of the whole item> }; returns the Dexie key
     * async get(id: any): Promise<T | undefined>  // decrypts _enc, merges the primary key back in
     * async put(item: T): Promise<any>
     * async delete(id: any): Promise<void>
     * async toArray(): Promise<T[]>
     * The raw row stored in IndexedDB MUST NOT contain any plaintext field value — only the primary key and the encrypted blob.

4. src/lib/crypto/index.ts — re-export the public API above.

5. Comprehensive Vitest tests in src/lib/crypto/*.test.ts covering: both derivation modes, round-trip encrypt/decrypt, wrong-key rejection, tampered-ciphertext rejection, fresh-IV behavior, and EncryptedTable ciphertext-at-rest + read-back. Use `// @vitest-environment node` in crypto tests so real WebCrypto is available, and `import 'fake-indexeddb/auto'` to back Dexie. Add fake-indexeddb to devDependencies (install via `corepack pnpm add -D fake-indexeddb`). Assertions must be real, not placeholders.

6. FIX the carried-over Phase 0 defect: .husky/pre-commit invokes bare `pnpm`, which fails on this corepack-only host. Change it to use `corepack pnpm` (or `npx`) so the hook runs. This is the only edit allowed to .husky/pre-commit.

HOW TO VERIFY before finishing (run from the REPO root): `corepack pnpm install`, `corepack pnpm run typecheck`, `corepack pnpm run test`, `corepack pnpm run lint` — all must exit 0. Fix failures only within your owned paths.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: make the changes in the owned paths, then write ./notes.md in your task directory: what you read, the files you created/changed, the exact commands you ran with results, the AES-GCM/PBKDF2 parameters chosen, how entropy is mixed in, and any assumption or Phase 2 follow-up (e.g. how the derived key/entropy will be persisted for re-login).

HARD RULES: match the API signatures exactly; never store plaintext at rest; never weaken a test to make it pass; keep the code boring, typed, and idiomatic; do not edit files outside your ownership; do not commit.
tasks.verified: A hidden orchestrator-owned contract test passes against the worker's crypto modules (two derivation modes, AES-GCM round-trip, wrong-key and tamper rejection, fresh IV, and EncryptedTable ciphertext-at-rest via Dexie/fake-indexeddb); PBKDF2>=100k and AES-GCM primitives are present; fake-indexeddb is a devDep; the Husky hook no longer calls bare pnpm; and typecheck + lint + the worker suite exit 0. Only owned paths changed; nothing committed.
